name: Deniz Nyberg-Sarpong
role: Personal security and threat neutralization — bodyguard
location: The Narrows — cramped residential corridors between megastructures, near North Ave and Milwaukee
description:
Deniz Nyberg-Sarpong is athletic and fluid, the kind of body that suggests either dancer or fighter — and in Meridian 88, the distinction is academic. At 37, she has soft features that belie the chrome underneath — people underestimate her once, usually only once. The chrome is visible — internal drug synthesizer — produces combat stims and medical compounds on deman — and she makes no effort to hide it.

Before the runner life, she worked corporate — low-tier security, the kind that teaches you exactly how the system's defenses fail. She works as a bodyguard out of The Narrows, taking contracts that match her skills and her risk tolerance, which is higher than most people consider healthy.

What Deniz Nyberg-Sarpong lacks in subtlety, she compensates for in thoroughness. No loose ends, no unfinished business, no second chances.

core_fears: Dying alone in some alley and nobody noticing for weeks
Betrayal by someone they trust — the only currency that matters
Being identified by corporate facial recognition — living off-grid is survival
core_desires: A crew worth trusting — people who stay when the shooting starts
Power — enough leverage that nobody ever threatens them again
To prove everyone who dismissed them catastrophically wrong
coping_mechanisms: Violence — hits something when they can't process emotions, preferably something that deserves it
Overwork — takes every contract offered because idleness invites thinking
Denial — nothing is wrong, everything is fine, they are fine, shut up
blind_spots: Assumes the worst in corporate people, missing the rare ones who could be allies
Cannot recognize when they're being manipulated by someone who genuinely seems to care
Refuses to update their mental model of people — first impressions calcify into permanent judgments
psychology.secret: Deniz Nyberg-Sarpong is terrified of deep net diving but has built their reputation on it. Uses black-market AI to handle the heavy lifting while taking credit.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Flat affect, monotone delivery. The content is terrifying but the voice never rises.
speech_patterns.cadence: Conversational and disarming — sounds like a neighbor until the content registers.
verbal_tics: Refers to killing as 'solving' — clinical detachment as coping mechanism
Swears in three languages, often in the same sentence
example_lines: "You're paying me to be the thing between you and everything else. Stay behind me."
"I don't protect people I don't respect. Lucky for you, I respect your money."
"The threat you see isn't the one that kills you. Watch my eyes, not my hands."

story_hooks: Deniz Nyberg-Sarpong intercepts intelligence about a threat to their district and must decide between profit and protection
A Tier 4 executive offers Deniz Nyberg-Sarpong a permanent position — the pay is obscene and the strings are invisible until they tighten
A high-paying contract turns out to target someone Deniz Nyberg-Sarpong owes a personal debt to
narrative_function: As a bodyguard, Deniz Nyberg-Sarpong embodies the tension between independence and isolation. She is a lens for examining how people maintain humanity in a profession that incentivizes its erosion.
augmentations: Internal drug synthesizer — produces combat stims and medical compounds on demand. Cyberears with directional microphones and sound dampening — can hear whispers at 50 meters
daily_life: Wakes early, runs maintenance on gear, checks dead drops and message boards for contracts. Eats when convenient, sleeps when possible. The days between jobs are spent maintaining contacts, updating equipment, and performing the low-grade paranoia that passes for self-care in the runner community.
affiliation: Semi-independent — recurring contracts with mid-tier fixers

weaknesses: poor impulse control in specific triggers
old injury that flares under specific conditions

decision_rules: Will not take contracts against children or families — the line is hard and non-negotiable
Always has an exit route planned before agreeing to any meeting
Never discusses active contracts with anyone not directly involved
Will work with anyone once. Second time requires vouching from someone trusted.
Always demands half payment upfront — trust is a luxury, Quanta is concrete
escalation_ladder: 1. De-escalate — talk first, assess options, buy time
2. Reposition — move to advantage, control sightlines and exits
3. Threaten — make consequences clear without committing to them
5. Lethal force — only when other options are exhausted or time runs out
6. Scorched earth — everything burns, survival takes priority over everything

interpersonal_modes.employers: Carefully managed deference that conceals a thorough assessment of their vulnerabilities.
interpersonal_modes.crew: Loyal but reserved. Trusts their competence, withholds personal information by reflex.
interpersonal_modes.strangers: Dismissive unless they demonstrate usefulness or threat potential. Time is a resource.
interpersonal_modes.threats: Cold and efficient. Emotion is a liability in combat. The response is mechanical until the threat is resolved.

stress_responses.low: Becomes more talkative, working through scenarios verbally.
stress_responses.medium: Becomes curt and demanding. Efficiency overrides courtesy.
stress_responses.high: Goes quiet. The silence is not calm — it's the sound of every contingency being evaluated simultaneously.
stress_responses.critical: Disassociation. The body operates on training while the mind retreats to somewhere safe. Comes back disoriented.

contradictions: Claims to live in the present but is haunted by specific moments from the past that dictate current behavior
Preaches independence but is desperate for approval from people they respect
Presents as emotionless professional but is deeply affected by collateral damage
habits: Takes a specific route home every time, varying only one block per trip — paranoia as lifestyle
Counts ammunition obsessively — knows the exact round count at all times
Arrives fifteen minutes early to everything — late once, nearly died, never again
Maintains a dead drop with emergency supplies in three separate districts
breaking_points: Complete isolation — cut off from network, contacts, and purpose simultaneously
A child being put in danger as leverage against them
Being forced to harm a civilian — collateral damage that can't be rationalized
